topology_reasoning: The reference is a four-port, orthogonal photonic junction/crossing. Four narrow rectangular ports enter from the left, right, top, and bottom, and each port expands through a smooth tapered transition into a rounded lobe. The four lobes overlap at a compact central junction; the overall footprint is symmetric about both horizontal and vertical axes. The function-defining knobs are the port guide width, the lobe maximum width, the flare/taper length, the lobe reach toward the center, and the amount of central overlap/rounding. I will model the lobes with parametric gf.Path centerlines and circular bends, then assemble the four rotated arms with primitives only on layer (1, 0).

iterations.change_made: Initial four-arm gf.Path extrusion; the width function was defined but the two-point path did not sample the lobe profile, so the raster was a narrow orthogonal cross.

Added 129 sampled points along the arm centerline so the vectorized width profile is actually extruded; the rounded four-lobe junction now matches the calibrated footprint and exceeded the 0.85 stop threshold.
